modules.title: Introduction
modules.description: Introduction to Data Science, including its definition, required skills, tools, data types, data collections, preprocessing, data analysis, and major types of analytics.
modules.overview: This module introduces the foundations of Data Science. It covers what Data Science is, the skills and tools needed for data science work, different data types and collections, data preprocessing, and the major approaches used for analysing data.
objectives: Understand the definition and fundamentals of Data Science.
Identify the skills and tools required for Data Science.
Understand different data types and data collections.
Explain data preprocessing and data analysis.
Differentiate descriptive, diagnostic, predictive, prescriptive, exploratory, and mechanistic analysis.

modules.title: Data Extraction
modules.description: Extracting meaning from data through feature selection, user retention, filters, wrappers, entropy, decision tree algorithms, random forests, the dimensionality problem, SVD, and PCA.
modules.overview: This module focuses on extracting useful information from data and selecting informative features. It introduces feature-selection approaches, decision trees, random forests, dimensionality problems, singular value decomposition, and principal component analysis.
objectives: Understand how useful meaning can be extracted from data.
Explain feature selection and feature-selection methods.
Understand entropy and decision tree algorithms.
Describe random forests and their use in data analysis.
Understand the dimensionality problem, SVD, and PCA.

modules.title: Data Visualization
modules.description: Visualizing data using Matplotlib, Pandas, Seaborn, line plots, bar plots, histograms, density plots, scatter plots, facet grids, and categorical data visualizations.
modules.overview: This module introduces Python-based data visualization. It covers the Matplotlib API, plotting with Pandas and Seaborn, and a range of plots for understanding distributions, relationships, and categorical data.
objectives: Understand the basic Matplotlib API.
Create visualizations using Pandas and Seaborn.
Represent data using line plots, bar plots, histograms, and density plots.
Create scatter plots and facet grids.
Visualize categorical data effectively.

modules.title: Statistical Thinking
modules.description: Understanding distributions through histograms, outliers, variance, probability mass functions, cumulative distribution functions, percentile-based statistics, random numbers, and probability distributions.
modules.overview: This module develops statistical thinking for understanding and representing data distributions. It covers histograms, outliers, variance, PMFs, CDFs, percentile-based statistics, random numbers, and important probability distributions including exponential, normal, and lognormal distributions.
objectives: Represent and plot distributions using histograms.
Identify outliers and summarize distributions.
Understand variance and probability mass functions.
Represent and interpret cumulative distribution functions and percentile-based statistics.
Understand exponential, normal, and lognormal distributions.

modules.title: Time Series Analysis and Predictive Modeling
modules.description: Analysing time series through importing and cleaning data, plotting, moving averages, missing values, serial correlation, autocorrelation, predictive modeling, model evaluation, model-solution building, and sentiment analysis.
modules.overview: This module introduces time series analysis and predictive modeling. It covers importing and cleaning time-series data, plotting and moving averages, handling missing values, serial correlation and autocorrelation, predictive modeling, evaluation of predictive models, building predictive model solutions, and sentiment analysis.
objectives: Import, clean, and plot time-series data.
Understand moving averages and missing values in time series.
Explain serial correlation and autocorrelation.
Understand predictive modeling and evaluate predictive models.
Build predictive model solutions and understand sentiment analysis.

subExperiments.name: CSV File Handling
subExperiments.description: Read an online CSV dataset, write CSV output, and work with tab-delimited student data.
subExperiments.code:
import pandas as pd
import os

# 1A.1 - Read CSV file (cached locally for instant loading, with online fallback)
url = "https://raw.githubusercontent.com/mwaskom/seaborn-data/master/iris.csv"
if os.path.exists("iris.csv"):
    df = pd.read_csv("iris.csv")
else:
    try:
        df = pd.read_csv(url)
    except Exception:
        df = pd.read_csv("students.csv")
print("First five rows of the dataset:")
print(df.head())
print("\nDataset Information:")
print(df.info())
print("\nNumber of rows and columns:")
print(df.shape)

# 1A.2 - Write the DataFrame to CSV
output_file = "iris_output.csv"
df.to_csv(output_file, index=False)
print(f"\nThe dataset has been successfully written to {output_file}")

# 1A.3 - Create a tab-delimited student file, then read it
student_data = {
    "Roll_No": [101, 102, 103, 104],
    "Name": ["Anusha", "Babitha", "Charitha", "Deepika"],
    "Department": ["IT", "IT", "CSE", "ECE"],
    "Percentage": [89, 92, 88, 85]
}
student_df = pd.DataFrame(student_data)
student_df.to_csv("students.txt", sep="\t", index=False)
print("\nData successfully written to students.txt")

print("\nStudent data read from the tab-delimited file:")
print(pd.read_csv("students.txt", sep="\t"))

subExperiments.name: SQLite Database Operations
subExperiments.description: Create a SQLite table, insert records, query them with Pandas, then update and delete a record.
subExperiments.code:
import sqlite3
import pandas as pd

conn = sqlite3.connect("students.db")
cursor = conn.cursor()

cursor.execute("""CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS students
                  (id INTEGER, name TEXT)""")
cursor.execute("INSERT INTO students VALUES (1, 'John')")
conn.commit()

df = pd.read_sql_query("SELECT * FROM students", conn)
print(df)

cursor.execute("UPDATE students SET name = 'Alice' WHERE id = 1")
cursor.execute("DELETE FROM students WHERE id = 1")
conn.commit()
conn.close()

experiments.name: Web Scraping and Exploratory Data Analysis of Product Reviews
experiments.description: Extract product reviews from web pages using Beautiful Soup, perform NLP text analysis, generate WordClouds for positive and negative reviews, compute text statistics distributions, and perform VADER sentiment analysis.

subExperiments.name: Extract Product Reviews with Beautiful Soup
subExperiments.description: Extract customer review titles, bodies, and ratings from an authorized HTML source using Beautiful Soup and save to CSV.
subExperiments.code:
from bs4 import BeautifulSoup import pandas as pd import os # Experiment 8A: Web Scraping Product Reviews using Beautiful Soup # Reads authorized/saved reviews.html and extracts title, review text, and rating html_file = "reviews.html" if not os.path.exists(html_file): print("reviews.html not found, using default sample HTML.") html_content = """
Great product
5 out of 5
Excellent quality! Works like a charm and very durable. I am extremely satisfied with this purchase.
Not satisfied
2 out of 5
The product stopped working after three days. Very poor build and terrible customer service.
Worth buying
4 out of 5
Good performance and decent battery life. Fast delivery and nice packaging. Satisfied!
""" else: with open(html_file, "r", encoding="utf-8") as file: html_content = file.read() soup = BeautifulSoup(html_content, "html.parser") review_blocks = soup.select(".review") records = [] for block in review_blocks: review_element = block.select_one(".review-text") rating_element = block.select_one(".rating") title_element = block.select_one(".review-title") review_text = review_element.get_text(" ", strip=True) if review_element else "" rating_text = rating_element.get_text(" ", strip=True) if rating_element else "" title = title_element.get_text(" ", strip=True) if title_element else "" if review_text: records.append({ "title": title, "review": review_text, "rating": rating_text }) df = pd.DataFrame(records) df.to_csv("product_reviews.csv", index=False, encoding="utf-8-sig") print(df.head()) print("\nTotal reviews extracted:", len(df)) print("Saved to product_reviews.csv")

subExperiments.name: WordCloud Analysis for Reviews
subExperiments.description: Classify reviews using VADER compound polarity and generate WordCloud visualizations for all, positive, and negative reviews.
subExperiments.code:
import pandas as pd
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import os
try:
    from wordcloud import WordCloud
except ImportError:
    from server.wordcloud import WordCloud
from vaderSentiment.vaderSentiment import SentimentIntensityAnalyzer

# Experiment 8B(i): WordCloud Generation for All, Positive, and Negative Reviews

# Ensure product_reviews.csv exists
if not os.path.exists("product_reviews.csv"):
    df_init = pd.DataFrame({
        "title": ["Great product", "Not satisfied", "Worth buying", "Waste of money", "Outstanding performance"],
        "review": [
            "Excellent quality! Works like a charm and very durable. Extremely satisfied.",
            "The product stopped working after three days. Very poor build and terrible customer service.",
            "Good performance and decent battery life. Fast delivery and nice packaging.",
            "Bad experience. Broken on arrival and unusable. Cheap plastic parts.",
            "Amazing device! Exceeded my expectations. Beautiful design, super fast, and wonderful display."
        ],
        "rating": ["5 out of 5", "2 out of 5", "4 out of 5", "1 out of 5", "5 out of 5"]
    })
    df_init.to_csv("product_reviews.csv", index=False)

df = pd.read_csv("product_reviews.csv")
df["review"] = df["review"].fillna("").astype(str)

analyzer = SentimentIntensityAnalyzer()

def classify_sentiment(text):
    score = analyzer.polarity_scores(text)["compound"]
    if score >= 0.05:
        return "Positive"
    elif score <= -0.05:
        return "Negative"
    return "Neutral"

df["sentiment"] = df["review"].apply(classify_sentiment)

def generate_wordcloud(text, title, filename):
    if not text.strip():
        print(f"No text available for: {title}")
        return

    cloud = WordCloud(
        width=1200,
        height=600,
        background_color="white",
        max_words=150,
        collocations=False
    ).generate(text)
    
    plt.figure(figsize=(12, 6))
    plt.imshow(cloud, interpolation="bilinear")

subExperiments.code:
import re
import pandas as pd
import nltk
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import seaborn as sns
from nltk.corpus import stopwords
from collections import Counter
import os

# Experiment 8B(ii): Distribution of Stopwords, Numerics, Word Count, Character Count, and Avg Word Length

nltk.download("stopwords", quiet=True)

if not os.path.exists("product_reviews.csv"):
    df_init = pd.DataFrame({
        "title": ["Great product", "Not satisfied", "Worth buying"],
        "review": [
            "Excellent quality with 10 days battery life and 100 percent satisfaction.",
            "Defective 2 items received out of 5 ordered. Completely broken.",
            "Good value for 2026. Highly recommended!"
        ],
        "rating": ["5 out of 5", "1 out of 5", "4 out of 5"]
    })
    df_init.to_csv("product_reviews.csv", index=False)

df = pd.read_csv("product_reviews.csv")
df["review"] = df["review"].fillna("").astype(str)

stop_words = set(stopwords.words("english"))

def analyze_review(text):
    tokens = re.findall(r"\b[\w']+\b", text.lower())
    words = re.findall(r"\b[A-Za-z]+\b", text)
    numeric_tokens = re.findall(r"\b\d+(?:\.\d+)?\b", text)

    stopword_tokens = [token for token in tokens if token in stop_words]

    return pd.Series({
        "word_count": len(tokens),
        "character_count": len(text),
        "numeric_count": len(numeric_tokens),
        "stopword_count": len(stopword_tokens),
        "average_word_length": (
            sum(len(word) for word in words) / len(words)
            if words else 0
        )
    })

statistics = df["review"].apply(analyze_review)
df = pd.concat([df, statistics], axis=1)

df.to_csv("review_statistics.csv", index=False)

columns = [
    ("stopword_count", "Stopword Count"),
    ("numeric_count", "Numeric Token Count"),
    ("word_count", "Word Count"),
    ("character_count", "Character Count"),
    ("average_word_length", "Average Word Length")
]

fig, axes = plt.subplots(3, 2, figsize=(14, 15))
axes = axes.flatten()

for i, (column, title) in enumerate(columns):
    sns.histplot(data=df, x=column, kde=True, ax=axes[i], bins=15, color="#7c3aed")
    axes[i].set_title(title, fontweight="bold")
    axes[i].set_xlabel(title)
    axes[i].set_ylabel("Number of Reviews")

axes[-1].axis("off")
plt.tight_layout()
plt.savefig("review_statistics_distributions.png", dpi=300)
plt.show()

all_tokens = re.findall(r"\b[\w']+\b", " ".join(df["review"]).lower())
stopword_frequency = Counter(token for token in all_tokens if token in stop_words)

print("Top 10 stopwords:")
print(stopword_frequency.most_common(10))

print("\nDescriptive statistics:")
print(df[[
    "stopword_count",
    "numeric_count",
    "word_count",
    "character_count",
    "average_word_length"
]].describe())

subExperiments.description: Calculate positive, negative, neutral, and compound scores and compare sentiment categories using NLTK VADER and standalone VADER.
subExperiments.code:
import pandas as pd
import nltk
from nltk.sentiment.vader import SentimentIntensityAnalyzer as NLTKVADER
from vaderSentiment.vaderSentiment import SentimentIntensityAnalyzer as StandaloneVADER
import os

# Experiment 8B(iii): Display Sentiment Values Using NLTK and VADER

nltk.download("vader_lexicon", quiet=True)

if not os.path.exists("product_reviews.csv"):
    df_init = pd.DataFrame({
        "title": ["Great", "Bad", "Okay"],
        "review": ["The product is excellent.", "The quality is terrible.", "The product is okay."],
        "rating": ["5 out of 5", "1 out of 5", "3 out of 5"]
    })
    df_init.to_csv("product_reviews.csv", index=False)

df = pd.read_csv("product_reviews.csv")
df["review"] = df["review"].fillna("").astype(str)

nltk_analyzer = NLTKVADER()
vader_analyzer = StandaloneVADER()

def classify(score):
    if score >= 0.05:
        return "Positive"
    elif score <= -0.05:
        return "Negative"
    return "Neutral"

# NLTK VADER scores
nltk_scores = df["review"].apply(nltk_analyzer.polarity_scores)
df["nltk_positive"] = nltk_scores.apply(lambda x: x["pos"])
df["nltk_negative"] = nltk_scores.apply(lambda x: x["neg"])
df["nltk_neutral"] = nltk_scores.apply(lambda x: x["neu"])
df["nltk_compound"] = nltk_scores.apply(lambda x: x["compound"])

# Standalone VADER scores
vader_scores = df["review"].apply(vader_analyzer.polarity_scores)
df["vader_positive"] = vader_scores.apply(lambda x: x["pos"])
df["vader_negative"] = vader_scores.apply(lambda x: x["neg"])
df["vader_neutral"] = vader_scores.apply(lambda x: x["neu"])
df["vader_compound"] = vader_scores.apply(lambda x: x["compound"])

df["nltk_sentiment"] = df["nltk_compound"].apply(classify)
df["vader_sentiment"] = df["vader_compound"].apply(classify)

# Display sample results
print(df[[
    "review",
    "nltk_compound",
    "nltk_sentiment",
    "vader_compound",
    "vader_sentiment"
]].head(10).to_string(index=False))

print("\nNLTK sentiment distribution:")
print(df["nltk_sentiment"].value_counts())

print("\nStandalone VADER sentiment distribution:")
print(df["vader_sentiment"].value_counts())

df.to_csv("sentiment_analysis_results.csv", index=False)
print("\nResults saved to sentiment_analysis_results.csv")

import pandas as pd
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import seaborn as sns
from sklearn.cluster import KMeans
from sklearn.preprocessing import StandardScaler
from sklearn.metrics import silhouette_score

# Reproducible customer personality sample dataset
df = pd.DataFrame({
    "Income": [25000, 28000, 32000, 35000, 42000, 45000, 52000, 58000, 65000, 70000, 78000, 85000, 92000, 105000, 115000, 125000],
    "MntWines": [15, 20, 25, 30, 45, 55, 80, 100, 130, 150, 180, 210, 230, 260, 300, 330],
    "MntFruits": [5, 8, 7, 10, 12, 15, 18, 20, 25, 28, 30, 35, 38, 42, 45, 50],
    "MntMeatProducts": [10, 15, 20, 25, 30, 40, 55, 65, 75, 90, 110, 125, 140, 160, 180, 200],
    "MntFishProducts": [3, 4, 5, 6, 8, 10, 12, 15, 18, 20, 24, 28, 30, 35, 40, 45],
    "MntSweetProducts": [4, 5, 6, 7, 9, 12, 14, 17, 20, 22, 25, 29, 32, 36, 40, 44],
    "MntGoldProds": [8, 10, 12, 15, 18, 22, 28, 32, 38, 42, 48, 52, 58, 65, 70, 78]
})
features = ["Income", "MntWines", "MntFruits", "MntMeatProducts", "MntFishProducts", "MntSweetProducts", "MntGoldProds"]
data = df[features].copy()
data = data.fillna(data.median())
X = StandardScaler().fit_transform(data)

scores = {}
for k in range(2, min(6, len(df))):
    labels = KMeans(n_clusters=k, random_state=42, n_init=10).fit_predict(X)
    scores[k] = silhouette_score(X, labels)
best_k = max(scores, key=scores.get)
model = KMeans(n_clusters=best_k, random_state=42, n_init=10)
df["Customer_Segment"] = model.fit_predict(X)

summary = df.groupby("Customer_Segment")[features].mean().round(2)
print("Silhouette scores:", {k: round(v, 3) for k, v in scores.items()})
print("\nBest number of clusters:", best_k)
print("\nCustomer segment summary:")
print(summary)
sns.scatterplot(data=df, x="Income", y="MntWines", hue="Customer_Segment", palette="Set2", s=90)
plt.title("Customer Segments by Income and Wine Spending")

from sklearn.feature_extraction.text import CountVectorizer
from sklearn.naive_bayes import MultinomialNB

# Sample labeled messages
texts = [
    "I am happy", "I feel joyful", "This is wonderful",

    "I feel sad", "I am lonely", "I miss my friend",
    "I love this", "You are so kind", "I adore my family"
]

    "happy", "happy", "happy",

    "love", "love", "love"
]

subExperiments.name: TF-IDF Emotion Detection with Emoji Prediction
subExperiments.description: Train a TF-IDF and Logistic Regression pipeline, evaluate it with a classification report, and display a relevant emoji for each predicted emotion.
subExperiments.code:
import pandas as pd
from sklearn.model_selection import train_test_split
from sklearn.pipeline import Pipeline
from sklearn.feature_extraction.text import TfidfVectorizer
from sklearn.linear_model import LogisticRegression
from sklearn.metrics import accuracy_score, classification_report

# Small, balanced sample dataset; use a larger labeled dataset for real applications
data = {
    "text": [
        "I am very happy today", "This is a wonderful day", "I feel cheerful and excited",
        "I am sad and lonely", "I feel very disappointed", "I miss my family so much",
        "I am angry with you", "This makes me furious", "I hate this situation",
        "I am scared of the dark", "I am afraid of losing", "I feel nervous and frightened",
        "I love you so much", "You mean everything to me", "I adore spending time with you", "I love my family",
        "Wow this is unbelievable", "I did not expect this surprise", "What an amazing unexpected gift"
    ],
    "emotion": [
        "happy", "happy", "happy", "sadness", "sadness", "sadness",
        "anger", "anger", "anger", "fear", "fear", "fear",
        "love", "love", "love", "love", "surprise", "surprise", "surprise"
    ]
}
df = pd.DataFrame(data)
X_train, X_test, y_train, y_test = train_test_split(
    df["text"], df["emotion"], test_size=0.33, random_state=42, stratify=df["emotion"]
)
model = Pipeline([
    ("tfidf", TfidfVectorizer(ngram_range=(1, 2)),
    ),
    ("classifier", LogisticRegression(max_iter=1000, random_state=42))
])
model.fit(X_train, y_train)
predictions = model.predict(X_test)
print("Test accuracy:", round(accuracy_score(y_test, predictions) * 100, 2), "%")
print("\nClassification report:")
print(classification_report(y_test, predictions, zero_division=0))

emoji_map = {"happy": "😊", "sadness": "😢", "anger": "😠", "fear": "😨", "love": "❤️", "surprise": "😲"}
def detect_emotion(text):
    emotion = model.predict([text])[0]
    print(f"Input text: {text}")
    print(f"Detected emotion: {emotion}")
    print(f"Relevant emoji: {emoji_map[emotion]}\n")

detect_emotion("I am happy to see you")
detect_emotion("I feel lonely today")
detect_emotion("I love my family")
